text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍ

words.gloss_range: opening conjunction/resumption particle linking the Moses proof-scene to the preceding argument
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a connected restart, not as a loose historical connector. It carries the prior warning pattern into a named Moses proof-scene and lets the new clause remain part of the same argument while narrowing into a concrete instance. Because it stands before the emphatic certainty frame, the scene change arrives already tied to proof, not as detached narration.

topics.headline: connected restart into Moses proof-scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the Moses episode as a resumed specification of the previous warning pattern, not a disconnected narrative insert.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a conjunction, and the CRITICAL rows converge on resumption that scopes over the full emphatic sending clause.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām attached to the certainty frame over the completed sending clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) tightens the resumed scene into formal confirmation. Its prefixed shape fastens emphasis onto the following certainty particle, so the whole mission claim, including the later evidence phrase, is heard as attested before the envoy and credentials are listed. The particle therefore marks a shift from connected report to an oath-answer-like proof-register.

topics.headline: resumption becomes attestation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sending as a certified premise rather than an ordinary narrative event.
topics.reason: Attachment translation support explicitly treats the lām plus following particle as an emphatic certainty frame over the sending verb.

words.gloss_range: certification particle before a perfect verb; local force is realized confirmation, not possibility
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) places certification outside the verb but immediately before it, making the dispatch an already realized fact. Its possible modal range is locally narrowed by the emphatic lām and perfect verb: here it does not suggest mere possibility. The ayah can therefore move from secured sending to envoy and proof-equipment instead of arguing whether the event occurred.

topics.headline: sending is treated as realized fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader starts from accomplished dispatch before the evidence list unfolds.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place the particle before a perfect verb inside an emphatic certainty frame.

topics.headline: confirmation, not possibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not misread the particle as leaving the mission speculative or only possible.
topics.reason: The broader particle range is narrowed because the local construction is lām plus particle plus perfect verb.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect first-person plural sending; completed divine commissioning of Moses with credentials
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatching, releasing, envoy and message-bearing; local Form IV selects commissioned dispatch rather than reciprocal correspondence or unmanaged release
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْسَلْنَا}} ({{tr:arsalnā}}) is the finite verb that carries the whole confirmed assertion: completed active sending with the divine speaker built into the suffix. It governs Moses as the object and then admits the evidence phrase, so mission is established before the credentials are named. The root can carry release and message-bearing pressure, but Form IV narrows that into controlled commissioning, not reciprocal exchange or self-propelled appearance; authority begins in the delegated sending before it appears as the warrant noun. The verb also creates forward momentum: the destination is not named until 40:24, so 40:23 completes the proof-equipment before the confrontation target appears. Its sending-with-signs pattern recalls Moses' sign-bearing confrontation in 7:103 and the wider messenger-sign thread that returns in 40:78.

topics.headline: completed divine dispatch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Moses' mission grammatically assigned to the divine sender, not to private initiative.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV perfect active first-person plural verb, and attachment evidence records Moses as its explicit object.

topics.headline: release becomes commissioned mission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels motion outward as authorized dispatch carrying a communicated charge, while the local form blocks unmanaged release or reciprocal correspondence.
topics.reason: The root family supports sending and release imagery, but the local Form IV verb with explicit object selects delegated commissioning.

topics.headline: verb organizes envoy, credentials, destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the clause as mission first, envoy second, credentials third, with the destination held for 40:24.
topics.reason: Attachment support notes that 40:24 supplies the dependent destination, while CRITICAL rows show the current verb controlling the envoy and evidence sequence.

topics.headline: Moses dispatch joins proof-bearing mission pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the compact local clause as part of the Moses-with-signs mission pattern, including 7:103, while still reading the local grammar first.
topics.reason: The intertext rows cite Moses-with-signs parallels such as 7:103 and same-surah messenger recurrence at 40:78.

words.gloss_range: foreign proper name as explicit direct object of the sending verb and carrier of the proof package
words.prose: {{ar:مُوسَىٰ}} ({{tr:mūsā}}) is the named object of the sending verb, so the credentials attach to a commissioned human envoy rather than floating as abstract proof. The proper name supplies recognition and definiteness without visible case ending; its accusative role is read from verb governance and sequence. The name also activates the Moses-with-signs confrontation pattern, including 7:103, 10:75, 23:45, and 11:96, while this ayah foregrounds the sender and proof-package before the opponent is named in 40:24.

topics.headline: named envoy receives the sending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the evidence package attached to a commissioned person, not left as detached proof-language.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the proper name the direct object of the sending verb.

topics.headline: recognition rather than root imagery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader takes the word's force from proper-name recognition and syntax rather than from an Arabic derivational image.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a foreign proper noun with no local Arabic root, and attachment evidence recovers its object role syntactically.

topics.headline: name cues proof-bearing confrontation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes Moses' name as a carrier of the familiar signs-and-authority mission formula, including 7:103 and 23:45.
topics.reason: CRITICAL rows cite recurring pairings of Moses with signs and authority in passages such as 7:103, 10:75, 23:45, and 11:96.

words.gloss_range: preposition binding the signs to the sending as instrument, accompaniment, and evidence complement
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the proof phrase to the sending verb. It directly governs the signs and, through coordination, keeps the authority term inside the same evidence orbit. Its contact value becomes evidentiary attachment: the signs are both means of confrontation and credentials carried with the mission, not a free-standing list after Moses' name. It also carries the clear-proofs frame from 40:22 into a specific evidence phrase after the envoy has been named.

topics.headline: preposition governs the proof package
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees signs and authority grammatically attached to the sending, not merely appended after the envoy.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the signs the complement of the preposition and makes the authority noun coordinated under the same proof frame.

topics.headline: proof travels with and works through mission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the evidence both accompanies Moses and functions as the mission's means of confrontation.
topics.reason: The local prepositional frame licenses instrument and accompaniment values without forcing only one.

topics.headline: general clear-proofs frame becomes specific signs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior proof discourse continue as a specific evidence phrase after the envoy is named.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL boundary rows tie this prepositional proof phrase to the preceding clear-proofs frame.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural signs as divinely sourced evidence units governed by the preposition
words.root_gloss_range: sign, mark, proof, wonder, and contested return/refuge pressure; local noun selects discrete evidentiary signs sourced by the speaker
words.prose: {{ar:ـَٔايَٰتِنَا}} ({{tr:āyātinā}}) gives the mission multiple proof-units while the suffix keeps their source singularly divine. The word is genitive under the preposition, so the signs function as attached instruments and credentials rather than a second direct object. The sign field makes each unit an indicator pressing toward response; the debated root pressure can add a return-to-source coloring, but it does not replace the local sign/proof sense. The sequence moves from these plural signs to singular authority, and the term joins a local proof thread that includes 40:13, 40:35, 40:56, 40:63, and 40:69.

topics.headline: many signs from one speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees evidence multiplied without its source being dispersed away from the sender.
topics.reason: QAC marks a plural noun with first-person plural possessive suffix, and the CRITICAL rows track the same speaker across verb and noun.

topics.headline: signs are mission equipment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads the signs as instruments and credentials attached to dispatch, not as an independent object beside Moses.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the noun as the complement governed by the preposition under the sending frame.

topics.headline: bounded indicators with return pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the signs are discrete proof-units that point back to their source and demand orientation, while local grammar keeps sign/proof as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The contested derivational pressure survives as coloring, but the local noun and evidence frame select signs as proof-units.

topics.headline: plural signs lead toward singular warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the evidence sequence move from plural observable indicators to a singular clarifying warrant, within the surah's repeated sign discourse at 40:13, 40:35, 40:56, 40:63, and 40:69.
topics.reason: CRITICAL rows tie the term to Moses-sign parallels such as 7:103 and to same-surah sign recurrence at 40:13, 40:35, 40:56, 40:63, and 40:69.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that adds authority as a second proof category under the evidence frame
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) attaches authority to the signs, not to Moses as a separate name or apposition. It preserves two proof nouns under one evidence frame: signs first, then warrant. Because the conjunction is prefixed to the authority noun, the second proof term arrives as coordinated from its first sound, making addition and escalation coincide.

topics.headline: signs plus authority stay distinct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the proof package accumulate from signs to warrant without collapsing the second noun into a mere explanation of the first.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the authority noun with the signs under the same proof frame, matching the CRITICAL rows on addition and escalation.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive proof-authority noun coordinated with the signs and qualified by manifest clarity
words.root_gloss_range: authority, proof, mandate, control, empowerment, and force; local phrase selects authorized warrant rather than raw coercion or an acting ruler

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accepted variant texture for the authority word without a shift in proof meaning

words.prose: {{ar:سُلْطَٰنٍۢ}} ({{tr:sulṭānin}}) is the second evidence noun, genitive within the proof orbit and indefinite as a kind of decisive warrant. Its root range includes authority, proof, mandate, and control-force, but the local adjective makes that power legible as authorized warrant rather than uncontrolled dominance. The noun pivots from plural signs to a singular warrant, then receives clarity as its own modifier. The variant {{ar:وَسُلُطَانٍ}} ({{tr:wa-suluṭānin}}) eases the heavy cluster without changing the proof meaning, and the tanwīn-to-mīm link binds authority audibly into clarity. Intertextually, 14:11's permission-only authority field is answered by Moses being sent with warrant here, while 40:35 and 40:56 later contrast disputed authority without warrant; 23:45 and 11:96 show the same mission-warrant formula.

topics.headline: authority is a credential, not an actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads authority as mission equipment within the evidence phrase, not as an independent agent or separate predicate.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the noun with the signs and records it as an indefinite genitive noun qualified by the following adjective.

topics.headline: power becomes manifest warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the force of authority and control, while the modifier keeps that force accountable to manifest proof rather than raw coercion.
topics.reason: The root range supports authority, power, and control, but the local phrase and adjective select a proof-authority reading.

topics.headline: singular warrant after plural signs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the proof sequence turn from multiple signs into one decisive warrant before the final clarity word.
topics.reason: The noun is singular and indefinite after a plural sign noun, and the following adjective directly qualifies it.

topics.headline: variant texture and nasal link bind authority to clarity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the authority word as recitationally compressed or eased, yet still joined to clarity by the noun-adjective sound surface.
topics.reason: The accepted variant changes recitational texture without shifting root meaning, and the tanwīn link is a surface payoff rather than a semantic override.

topics.headline: authorized warrant contrasts later disputed warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Moses' supplied warrant set against permission-only authority in 14:11 and later disputation without warrant in 40:35 and 40:56.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite 14:11, 40:35, 40:56, 23:45, and 11:96 as authority/warrant parallels and contrasts.

words.gloss_range: Form IV active participle used adjectivally; manifest and clarifying quality of the authority noun
words.root_gloss_range: separation, distinction, appearance, disclosure, and making clear; local participle selects manifest/clarifying authority rather than spatial interval or unrelated separation branches
words.prose: {{ar:مُّبِينٍ}} ({{tr:mubīnin}}) is the adjective locked to the authority noun by genitive indefiniteness, so clarity belongs to the warrant itself. As a Form IV active participle, it lets the authority be both manifest and clarifying: it stands out and separates proof from ambiguity. The ayah lands on this word, making disclosed intelligibility the final value after dispatch, envoy, signs, and authority; the paired genitive cadence makes authority and clarity sound like one closing unit. It also carries the proof root forward from 40:22 into a specific clarifying adjective here, while 40:35 later condemns dispute without arriving authority.

topics.headline: clarity qualifies the warrant itself
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees clarity as a property of the authority noun, not as a floating comment on the whole mission.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence says the adjective agrees with and qualifies the authority noun.

topics.headline: clarity separates proof from ambiguity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final adjective is not merely bright or emphatic; it makes authority legible by distinguishing truth from confusion.
topics.reason: V4 supports appearance, disclosure, and separation branches, while the local Form IV participial adjective selects manifest and clarifying force.

topics.headline: the proof sequence lands in clarity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah's final beat as disclosed intelligibility after the sequence of sending, envoy, signs, and authority.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows emphasize the final position, postposed adjective order, and paired cadence with the authority noun.

topics.headline: proof language returns as final adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the closing adjective with the proof vocabulary from 40:22 and the later positive-versus-disputed warrant contrast at 40:35.
topics.reason: CRITICAL rows tie the root to sign vocabulary, to 40:22's earlier clear proofs, to 2:256's distinction field, and to the 40:35 disputed-authority contrast.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ presents Moses as sent with two accompanying instruments.
baseline_models.mechanism: A commissioned bearer carries visible markers and a proof whose force lies in becoming manifest. Sending supplies the carrier relation, the signs supply publicly detectable marks, sultan supplies prevailing evidence, and mubin supplies disclosure.

activation_trace.role: The messenger-and-message image makes Moses the commissioned carrier of what follows.
The visible-mark image gives the mission publicly detectable signs rather than private information.
The prevailing-proof image gives the signs argumentative force.
The appearing-and-uncovering image makes that proof disclosed and inspectable.

changed_reading.before: God sent Moses with miracles and a clear proof.
changed_reading.after: God commissioned Moses as a carrier of publicly readable marks together with evidence able to prevail by being disclosed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَرْسَلْنَا and سُلْطَانٍ can form a dispatch-plus-jurisdiction construction, qualified by مُبِينٍ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sending releases Moses into action while sultan names conferred capacity or jurisdiction, not only an argument. Mubin makes the delegation publicly legible rather than tacit.

activation_trace.role: The dispatch-and-release image supplies movement into action in contrast to being held back.
The capacity-and-jurisdiction image supplies a delegated mandate accompanying the dispatch.
The uncovering image makes the mandate overt and recognizable.

changed_reading.after: Moses was released into the mission with an overtly conferred mandate to act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence سُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ permits the sharp-tongue branch of sultan to combine with the speech-disclosure branch of bayn.
baseline_models.mechanism: Authority can operate as forceful articulation: a carried message acquires an edge in speech and makes its meaning explicit. This coexists with, rather than replaces, the proof reading.

activation_trace.role: The carried-message image supplies content that must be voiced.
The sharp and forceful tongue image supplies verbal pressure and argumentative edge.
The disclosure-through-speech image turns verbal force into intelligible exposition.

changed_reading.before: The sultan is an object of proof that Moses possesses.
changed_reading.after: The sultan may also be the force of an articulated message that makes its own claim explicit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مُبِينٍ is anchored in a root that holds both separation and disclosure, immediately qualifying سُلْطَانٍ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The authority does not merely look clear; it performs distinction. Prevailing proof separates claims that had been entangled and then discloses the resulting boundary.

activation_trace.role: The prevailing-proof image supplies the force needed to decide between competing claims.
The separation image supplies the boundary-producing action of the criterion.
The explanatory disclosure image makes the produced distinction communicable.

changed_reading.before: Moses carries an evidently clear authority.
changed_reading.after: Moses carries an authority that actively separates rival claims and states the distinction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The delegated-authority baseline becomes a counter-sovereignty reading. God's exclusive kingdom and overpowering frame Pharaoh's presently visible rule, while Pharaoh claims to control what his people see and where they are guided. Moses' manifest sultan enters that occupied field as a rival authorization that exposes the ruler's self-certified vision.

activation_trace.role: The jurisdiction image anchors the focus mission as delegated authority.
The uncovering image makes the counter-authorization publicly visible.
The kingdom-and-sovereignty image supplies the encompassing authority within which every local rule is judged.
The overcoming-from-above image supplies ultimate supremacy behind the delegated mission.
The kingdom image locates Pharaoh's side in an explicitly present political dominion.
The ascendancy image supplies the regime's current outward upper hand.
The considered-opinion image shows Pharaoh making his own view the boundary of what others may see.
The gentle direction-to-a-path image supplies the guidance function Pharaoh claims to monopolize.

structural_cues: 40:24 names Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun as the immediate destination of the focus dispatch.
40:16 assigns kingdom to God, while 40:29 places present kingdom, visibility, seeing, and guidance in Pharaoh's speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two authority fields and Pharaoh's self-limiting formula of sight and guidance; I infer that the focus sultan is a counter-commission that makes his local supremacy answerable. A live alternative is that sultan remains proof only and contests his claims without denoting jurisdiction.

changed_reading.before: Moses receives a generally delegated authority.
changed_reading.after: Moses enters a regime of visible political dominance with a higher, publicly legible counter-authorization that challenges who may define sight and guidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus dispatch becomes one reopened link in a trace-bearing succession. Earlier missions leave marks that can be inspected; Joseph's clear proofs are followed by a declaration that no messenger will be dispatched after him; the surah later expands the series to recounted and unrecounted messengers. Sending Moses therefore contradicts an imagined closure while adding another visible historical trace.

activation_trace.role: The group-after-group image anchors the focus sending in a serial rather than isolated process.
The visible-marker image makes each dispatch capable of leaving a readable trace.
The lasting-mark image supplies historical residue by which former powers and encounters remain inspectable.
The disclosed-evidence image links Joseph's earlier proofs to the same visible mission pattern.
The dispatch-and-direction image supplies the explicitly denied possibility of a later mission.
The serial-messenger image turns the claim of no later messenger into an attempted terminal boundary.
The successive-dispatch image reopens and broadens the chain across many messengers.
The sequential-report image distinguishes narrated links from links left unnarrated while preserving one series.

structural_cues: 40:21 and 40:82 direct travel and inspection of earlier peoples' outcomes.
40:34 joins prior clear proofs to the claim that no messenger would be sent after Joseph; 40:78 explicitly states a larger sequence of sent messengers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lasting traces, an asserted end to dispatch after Joseph, and a larger messenger series; I infer that sending Moses functions as a reopening of a channel people declared closed. The live alternative is that 40:34 only diagnoses one community's attitude, though it still activates the recurring-series reading.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports the discrete historical sending of Moses.
changed_reading.after: The verse marks Moses as a new, trace-producing link in a succession whose supposed closure is itself contradicted by renewed dispatch.

context_deltas.mechanism: The discursive force attached to Moses' mission propagates through an unexpected social carrier. A believer inside Pharaoh's house moves from concealed belief to public speech, cites the clear proofs, and converts them into a conditional liar-versus-truthful test. The focus sultan is thus not only possessed by Moses; its argumentative edge can recruit and equip a secondary voice inside the opposing structure.

activation_trace.role: The forceful-tongue image anchors a discursive mode of the focus authority.
The speech-disclosure image anchors the authority's capacity to become an explicit argument.
The voiced-speech image supplies the insider's public relay of the case.
The hiding image establishes that the relay emerges from within a concealed social position.
The disclosure-by-sign-or-speech image makes Moses' proofs the content the insider rearticulates.
The contrary-to-truth image supplies one side of the insider's explicit evidentiary test.
The truthful-speech image supplies the opposing side of that test.

structural_cues: 40:28 begins with a man from Pharaoh's house who conceals belief, then gives direct speech centered on Moses' clear proofs.
The speech repeatedly tests the alternatives of Moses being a liar or truthful and assigns consequences to each.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an insider who cites Moses' proofs and voices a structured truth test; I infer that the mission's discursive authority has propagated into a secondary bearer. A live alternative is that the man independently constructs a prudential defense rather than transmitting the sultan itself.

changed_reading.before: The clear authority is an argumentative capacity located in Moses.
changed_reading.after: The mission's clear authority can become socially transmissible, generating a truth-testing voice from inside the regime it confronts.

context_deltas.mechanism: The separating-criterion baseline becomes procedural. God judges with what is fixed as true; opponents repeatedly twist themselves into dispute over the signs without any sultan having reached them; judgment is finally made between servants. Positive accompaniment by sultan at the focus therefore marks Moses' case as warranted, while mubin names an authority that can separate parties and claims.

activation_trace.role: The prevailing-proof image anchors the focus sultan as an evidentiary warrant.
The separation image anchors the warrant's power to distinguish claims.
The cutting-judgment image supplies the adjudicative endpoint of competing claims.
The fixed-and-reality-matching image supplies the standard by which judgment cuts.
The entwined-contention image supplies argument that is active but not thereby warranted.
The visible-marker image identifies the signs as the disputed evidentiary field.
The prevailing-proof image appears under explicit negation, marking the disputants' missing warrant.
The judgment-between-people image supplies the legal-social realization of separation.
The interval-between-parties image locates judgment across opposed sides.
The repeated entwined-contention image confirms that argumentative activity can persist without warrant.
The second explicit absence of prevailing proof sharpens the positive possession at the focus.

structural_cues: 40:35 and 40:56 repeat the same signs-dispute-without-sultan construction.
The focus says Moses is sent with sultan, producing an exact presence-versus-absence contrast.
40:20 joins judgment to truth, and 40:48 explicitly places judgment between servants.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies positive accompaniment at 40:23, repeated negative warrant in disputes, and judgment with truth between parties; I infer a procedural arrow from sultan to admissible claim and from mubin to discriminating judgment. A live alternative keeps sultan as delegated power rather than an evidentiary warrant.

changed_reading.before: Moses arrives with a clear proof that may win an argument.
changed_reading.after: Moses arrives with the warrant that makes his claim admissible in a field of unwarranted dispute, and that warrant functions as a criterion capable of separating claims and parties.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah separates manifest evidence from compulsory recognition. Signs can be denied with knowledge and treated as unrecognized even while remaining visible; only the later sight of overwhelming force produces a belated confession of belief. Mubin therefore describes disclosure on the side of the evidence, not an irresistible psychological effect on every recipient, and the focus sultan is distinguished from applied punishment.

activation_trace.role: The visible-marker image anchors the signs as available to recognition.
The appearing-and-uncovering image anchors manifestness on the evidence side.
The overpowering-force image supplies the possible coercive reading that the later sequence qualifies.
The visible-sign image remains present as the object of rejection.
The denial-despite-knowledge image shows that visibility need not produce acknowledgment.
The repeated visible-marker image makes recognition of signs an explicit question.
The contrary-to-recognition image supplies active nonacknowledgment of what is shown.

surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أَرْسَلْنَا activates dispatch as release in contrast to holding, while the mission's opponents answer released movement with seizure and restraint.

activation_trace.role: The dispatch-and-release image launches Moses into movement opposed to restraint.

strongest_changes: The repeated 'without sultan' disputes turn the focus possession of sultan into a warrant for admissible argument and discriminating judgment.

summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah repetition supplied unusually exact reversals around the compact focus phrase: with versus without sultan, visible proof versus refused recognition, dispatch versus capture, local kingdom versus higher authorization, and an allegedly closed messenger line versus renewed sending.
remaining_uncertainties: Sultan can still support proof, delegated jurisdiction, and forceful articulation simultaneously; the context sharpens their relations without forcing one lexical sense.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Authority is force released through disclosure.** `ر س ل/B001` gives being sent forth, `س ل ط/B001` coercive force let loose, and `ب ي ن/B001` separation. The coordinated signs and manifest authority assign the force an evidentiary form. I infer that disclosure separates viable from false claims and thereby empowers the envoy; authority reads as demonstrated capacity, not naked coercion.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Pharaoh’s tower project in 40:36–37 reveals the counter-use of “authority”: he tries to manufacture visible access when received manifest authority resists his control.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The messenger carries force in the form of proof.** Lexically, `س ل ط:B002` is "overpowering proof," distinct from its `B001` coercive force, while `ب ي ن:B005` is disclosing meaning by expression or sign. Structurally, the prior ayah says messengers arrived with clear demonstrations; 40:24 answers this disclosed authority with labels, and 40:25-26 escalates to killing. The authority's role is epistemic pressure that makes a case plain. The packet supplies proof followed by elite verbal and physical coercion; I infer that coercion substitutes for an inability to meet the proof on its own plane. Musa is therefore sent already empowered, though the power resides in manifest evidence rather than court control.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:35 and 40:56 define disputation precisely by the absence of `سلطان`; this retrospectively sharpens Musa's `س ل ط:B002` as warrant rather than coercive office.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem ülke yöneticisinin kullanabildiği gücü ve kendisine hak tanınan kişinin yetkisini hem de bu gücü taşıyan yöneticiyi belirtir. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu iki bağlı kullanımı doğru biçimde korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, salt güçlü kanıtı veya her tür kişisel yeterliliği değil, yönetmeye ya da tanınmış bir hakkı kullanmaya bağlı yetkiyi kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Sözcükleşme türü çözümlenmemiştir; tanım belirli bir yalın biçime bağlanmadan yetki ile yetki sahibinin kaynakta birlikte verilen anlamlarını korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir ülke yöneticisinin ya da kendisine belirli bir hak tanınmış kişinin kullanabildiği yönetme ve karar verme yetkisi; ayrıca bu yetkiyi taşıyan yöneticidir.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, ülkeyi yönetmeye veya tanınmış bir hakkı kullanmaya bağlı güç ve yetkidir.
Yetkinin adı, bu yetkiyi taşıyan yönetici kişi için de kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çerçevesi, ülke yönetimine veya tanınmış bir hakka dayanan yetkiyi ve bu yetkiyi taşıyan yöneticiyi aynı anlam alanında toplar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi akıcı ve keskin konuşmayı, söz söyleme gücünü, uzun dilliliği ve özellikle kadın için gürültülü çıkışmayı birlikte verir; kullanımın çoğunlukla yergi taşıdığını da belirtir. Dal çerçevesi bu bileşenleri doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Buradaki güç sözün akıcılığı, keskinliği ve gürültülü kullanımıyla sınırlıdır; siyasal ya da bedensel zorlama anlamı taşımaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem bağımsız biçimleri hem de dil ve konuşma çevresindeki yapılara bağlı kullanımları içerir; yapıya bağlı yergi ve uzun dillilik bütün yalın biçimlere genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Söz söylemede güçlü, akıcı ve keskin olma; bazı kullanımlarda özellikle bir kadının uzun dilli olup yüksek sesle çıkışmasıdır. Anlam çoğunlukla yergi taşır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, konuşmada akıcılık, söz gücü ve keskin dilliliktir.

Dil ve konuşma gücünü belirten yapıya bağlı kullanımlar çoğunlukla yergi bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar akıcı ve keskin dili ortak çekirdek olarak verir; kadınla ilgili kullanımlarda gürültülü çıkışma ve uzun dillilik öne çıkar, söz gücü anlatımı ise çoğunlukla yergi taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yağ anlamını ve aydınlatma işlevini destekler; ancak aktarımlar bunun genel bir yağ adı mı, belirli bir bitkisel yağ mı olduğu ve hangi bölgeye özgü sayıldığı konusunda ayrılır. Bu nedenle dal korunabilir, fakat tek ve tartışmasız bir yağ türü gibi sunulmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam aydınlatmada kullanılan bitkisel yağ çevresindedir; özellikle susam yağı sayılması ve bölgesel dağılımı kaynaklarda değişir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalın bir sözcük anlamıdır; tanım bu bağımsız yağ anlamını verir ve başka dallardaki güç ya da konuşma kullanımlarını içeri almaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tek bir uzunluk ve keskinlik birleşimi kurmaz: uzun ok ve bacaklar, anahtar dişleri, keskin uçlar, güçlü uzun toynak uçları ve sert toynak ayrı gerçekleşmelerdir. Dal korunabilir, ancak tanım bu özellikleri her örnekte birlikte bulunuyormuş gibi değil, uzunluk, keskinlik veya dayanıklı sertlik ailesi olarak vermelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Fiziksel özellik ailesi uzunluk, keskinlik ve sert dayanıklılığı kapsar; her nesnenin bu üç özelliğin tümünü taşıdığı ileri sürülmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem bağımsız biçimleri hem belirli nesne adlarına bağlı yapıları içerir; toynak ve keskin uç okumaları bütün yalın biçimlere genellenmeden ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Ok, kesici uç, anahtar dişi, bacak ve toynak gibi araç ya da beden parçalarında görülen belirgin uzunluk, keskinlik veya güçlü sertliktir. Bu özellikler farklı biçim ve yapılarda ayrı ayrı gerçekleşir.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, bir araç veya beden parçasında belirgin uzunluk, keskinlik ya da dayanıklı sertlik bulunmasıdır.
Bağımsız biçimler uzun okları, anahtar dişlerini ve uzun bacakları adlandırabilir.
Nesne adına bağlı yapılar keskin uçları, güçlü ve uzun toynak uçlarını ya da sert toynağı niteler.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak anlatımı uzun ok, anahtar dişi, keskin uç, uzun bacak, güçlü uzun toynak ucu ve sert toynak örneklerini verir; ortak alan tek bir özellik değil, uzunluk, keskinlik ve güçlü sertlik ailesidir.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal şeyin görünür ve anlaşılır hale gelmesiyle sınırlıdır; özel olarak sözlü anlatım değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam karma yapıdadır; kendiliğinden görünme, açıklığa kavuşturma ve belirli kanıt kalıpları ayrı facetlerde tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin gizlilikten veya belirsizlikten çıkıp görünür, anlaşılır ve açık hale gelmesidir; bu açıklık kanıt ya da açık işaret olarak da gerçekleşebilir.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam şeyin görünür, anlaşılır ve açık hale gelmesidir.

Açık kanıt, açık işaret veya belirgin belge olarak adlaşmış kullanımı vardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar görünme ve açıklığa kavuşma çekirdeğinde birleşir; bazı sözler açıklığı nesnede, bazıları onu açık hale getirme veya açık kanıt niteliğinde gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Görünür, anlaşılır ve açık hale gelme çekirdeğini kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Açığa çıkma, belirginleşme ve anlaşılır olma çekirdeğini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Açık gösterge ve kanıt niteliğini korur.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

missing_branch_inventories.reason: no accepted, non-contaminated branch inventory in resource

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

butuncul_okuma.note: no whole-surah reading file exists for this surah

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
